conventions: The receiver follows django.contrib.sites.management.create_default_site: signature (app_config, verbosity=2, interactive=True, using=DEFAULT_DB_ALIAS, apps=global_apps, **kwargs); apps.get_model in try/except LookupError; router.allow_migrate_model(using, Document); every read and write through .using(using) / objects.using(using); creation inside transaction.atomic(using=using). Connected in MvpComplianceConfig.ready() with post_migrate.connect(create_declared_documents, sender=self). Module mvp_compliance/management.py
declared_documents() in models.py returns getattr(settings, 'MVP_COMPLIANCE_DOCUMENTS', {}), read at the point of use like acceptances_survive_account_removal()

Validation runs on the GLOBAL Document model's fields: Document._meta.get_field('slug').clean(value, None) and the same for name. Also refuse a name that is empty or differs from name.strip(), a name another document has under a different slug, and a name two declarations share. Collect every fault, then raise one ImproperlyConfigured naming each declaration's slug and, for a clash, the other document's slug. Strings marked for translation
Tests assert ImproperlyConfigured by type and by the slugs the message contains, never by its sentence
Test module for management.py is tests/test_management.py; the migrate-wiring test goes in tests/test_app.py
seed_demo: set the kind of a document it is about to seed AFTER the early return for a document that already has versions (seed_demo.py around line 519)
Docs: a refused declaration leaves the migrations applied; running migrate again after fixing the settings completes what was skipped. migrate shows the message in English (@no_translations)
Repo standards that reviews have missed before: no leading-underscore names anywhere; line length 88; no compatibility aliases; no test of text content or wording; no test of layout or appearance
A mechanism an experienced Django developer would recognise beats a clever one: no dataclass, registry or settings object
Every user-facing string is wrapped for translation and none says 'compliant', 'compliance' or names a regulation
Text for docs is written for an outside contributor: plain words, no mention of agents, stages or tooling
